newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Police capture more Hondurans who burned jail, fled.
newsitem.headline: Police capture more Hondurans who burned jail, fled.

text.p: Police and troops on Tuesday searched for more than 200 prisoners, some of them dangerous felons, who escaped from a crowded Honduras jail following a riot that nearly destroyed the prison.
Some 232 prisoners were on the loose after 482 of them broke free late on Monday from a facility near Santa Barbara, 110 miles (180 kilometres) northwest of Tegucigalpa, the capital, police said.

"Police patrols and the army have recaptured 250 of the inmates and are continuing to search for the remainder at large," Interior Minister Efrain Moncada, who is in charge of the country's internal security, told a news conference.
The army set up roadblocks and police searched homes in nearby villages for the escaped criminals, who threw rocks at guards and set fire to the jail before breaking out.
One prisoner was killed during the melee, although police had no details about how he died.

The inmates were angry at squalid prison conditions and a slow judicial system in Honduras, a nation that has left about 90 percent of prisoners languishing in jail without a formal sentence, according to official statistics.

"People are protesting because they suspended our daily visits and we live in bad conditions, there is hardly any room to stand in here," one inmate who identified himself as Cristobal Sagastume told Honduran radio late on Monday.
Television showed the charred remains of the prison, which burned down almost entirely because there was no fire department in Santa Barbara, a town of some 35,000 residents.
Witnesses said villagers used water hoses and buckets to help douse the flames until firefighters arrived from the city of San Pedro Sula, a three-hour drive away.
Inmates also rioted and set a fire to another jail on Monday in the town of Trujillo, 180 miles (290 km) north of the capital, but officials said no prisoners had escaped or were injured.
Authorities on Tuesday said they had regained control of the Trujillo jail, but admitted that the riots were likely to raise questions about the overtaxed judicial system.
"Our penitentiary system is an anachronism. The buildings to house prisoners were built last century and cannot cope," Romelia Garcia, the head of the prison system, told reporters.
Moncada, the interior minister, told reporters that the government was considering taking measures to reduce overcrowding such as granting more prisoners conditional release.
